text:
acme-cs: Hey team — our service on Dedicated EU is seeing intermittent 502s and p99 spiking to ~2.5s on /v1/generate. Sample request ID: rq_20260317_abc123. First seen ~2026-03-17 14:12 UTC. Can you pull a repro and logs?

lisa-support: Thanks — sorry you're hitting this. Can you confirm the model + exact route you hit and whether this is happening on a single customer cluster or across multiple clusters? Also, if you have a curl repro that would help a lot.

acme-cs: Route is POST /v1/generate (model: redwood-13b-v2). Only on our dedicated-eu cluster (customer-id: acme-inc). I do have a curl that fails ~30% of the time:

```bash
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-acme-XXXX" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -d '{"model":"redwood-13b-v2","input":"Summarize this...","max_tokens":64}' -i
```

When it fails we get: HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
Request-ID: rq_20260317_abc123

ben-sre: Thanks — that request ID is useful. I'm going to collect the cluster debug bundle and pod logs. Can you confirm the approximate window (14:10-14:15 UTC ok)? Also paste the node name if you have it (kubectl node list from your side) or I can surface the nodes we saw handling your customer traffic.

acme-cs: Yes 14:10-14:15 is the main window. Node we saw in our monitoring is node-eu-3 (but that might be a L7 node).

lisa-support: Ok, I'm kicking off an internal debug bundle request now. Debug-bot, please create bundle for cluster dedicated-eu for window 2026-03-17T14:08:00Z to 2026-03-17T14:20:00Z and include: kube pod logs (inference, router, autoscaler), node syslog, dmesg, nvidia-smi output, container metrics.

debug-bot: Created debug bundle request id: dbg-987654. ETA ~8 minutes. Includes: pod logs (namespaces: redwood-inference), node metrics (nvidia-smi snapshots), condensed tracer traces (sampling).

noah-eng-runtime: While we wait, can you run a targeted capture on your side to reproduce? Two quick things that help root cause: 1) a curl with verbose headers to capture gateway span/trace, 2) the raw request payload that triggers the 502. Also, if you can run the same curl but add header X-Rw-Debug: 1 that should cause our router to emit a trace id in the response headers. Example:

```bash
curl -v -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-acme-XXXX" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "X-Rw-Debug: 1" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-13b-v2","input":"Summarize this...","max_tokens":64}' -i
```

When it fails you should see a header like: Rw-Trace: trace-0a1b2c4d. Paste that trace id here.

acme-cs: Ran that now — when it 502'd I got header: Rw-Trace: trace-0a1b2c4d. Attached curl output snippet.

lisa-support: Great — trace id + request id = good triangulation. ben, can you pull logs for trace-0a1b2c4d and rq_20260317_abc123? Also please run kubectl describe pod on the inference pod that served the request and collect container restart counts.

ben-sre: On it. Commands I'm running (for internal reference / what I'll paste into the bundle):

```bash
kubectl -n redwood-inference get pods -o wide --selector=app=inference
POD                       READY   STATUS    RESTARTS   AGE   NODE
inference-7f5c9bd4-pt9k    1/1     Running   2          3d    node-eu-3

kubectl -n redwood-inference logs inference-7f5c9bd4-pt9k --previous > /tmp/inference-prev.log
kubectl -n redwood-inference logs inference-7f5c9bd4-pt9k > /tmp/inference-current.log
kubectl -n redwood-inference describe pod inference-7f5c9bd4-pt9k > /tmp/inference-describe.txt

# collect node-level GPU and kernel messages
ssh core@node-eu-3 'sudo nvidia-smi -q -d PERFORMANCE > /tmp/node-eu-3-nvidia.txt; sudo dmesg | tail -n 300 > /tmp/node-eu-3-dmesg.txt'

# collect kubelet and syslog around incident window
sudo journalctl -u kubelet --since "2026-03-17 14:05:00" --until "2026-03-17 14:20:00" > /tmp/kubelet-window.log
sudo journalctl --since "2026-03-17 14:05:00" --until "2026-03-17 14:20:00" | grep -i -E "oom|fail|nvidia|gpu|error" > /tmp/syslog-errors.txt
```

ben-sre: Findings so far: inference container had 2 restarts in the last 72h. Previous container restart at 2026-03-17T02:11Z due to OOMKilled (heap growth pattern) but no OOM during the 14:10 window. dmesg on node-eu-3 shows repeated GPU driver WARN lines ~14:11:30: "NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 79, GPU has fallen off the bus" — that's a GPU error we should pay attention to. Collected nvidia-smi snapshot shows GPU temp 76C, memory usage 48%, running processes include inference runtime and a maintenance job.

lisa-support: That GPU Xid 79 is commonly transient but can cause a short tail-latency blip or dropped connections. We'll correlate with router logs. noah — any known issues with the driver version on node-eu-3?

noah-eng-runtime: node-eu-3 is running driver 515.76 with cudnn 8.3 per our inventory. We did a rolling kernel patch last week on eu nodes which is known to expose an infrequent Xid 79 regresssion with that driver+kernel combo. Not widespread but plausible. Steps: 1) check for PCI reset events in dmesg around the Xid times, 2) check if the runtime reconnected KV cache or re-established the gRPC stream to the router. If the connection dropped mid-stream, that yields 502s at the gateway.

acme-cs: Anything we need to run on our side? We can throttle traffic or pin to another cluster but would prefer a fix.

lisa-support: Two immediate remediation options: A) drain node-eu-3 (kubectl drain) and move pods off this node if you prefer an immediate mitigation, or B) apply our kernel-driver compatibility micro-patch (we can schedule ASAP) and then restart the host services. We need your permission for an orchestrated drain if you want to go that route.

acme-cs: Please drain node-eu-3 now — we want to avoid more 502s while you investigate.

ben-sre: Acknowledged — draining. Command and steps I ran:

```bash
kubectl drain node-eu-3 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
# verify pods evicted and new pods scheduled on node-eu-1/eu-2
kubectl -n redwood-inference get pods -o wide --selector=app=inference
```

ben-sre: Drain completed. All inference pods rescheduled within 60s onto node-eu-1 and node-eu-2. Monitoring p99 now — initial trend down to ~220ms.

lisa-support: I've attached the debug bundle dbg-987654 to this thread (link internal-only). Bundle includes: /tmp/inference-current.log, /tmp/inference-prev.log, /tmp/inference-describe.txt, /tmp/node-eu-3-dmesg.txt, /tmp/node-eu-3-nvidia.txt, kubelet window logs, and traced spans for trace-0a1b2c4d.

noah-eng-runtime: From spans we see a router -> runtime gRPC timeout at 14:11:37 with status UNAVAILABLE and a TCP reset on the server side. That aligns with the Xid 79 timeframe. We'll open a maintenance ticket to schedule the kernel-driver micro-patch and will follow up here with timeline.

acme-cs: Thanks — appreciate the quick help and the drain. Please keep us posted on remediation.

lisa-support: Will do. Next steps for us: (1) eng-runtime to schedule patch and post ETA, (2) SRE to monitor for repeat Xid events in the next 24h, (3) support to keep this thread updated and close once patch applied and no recurrence for 24h. I'll mark this high priority. :thumbsup:

ben-sre: Adding watch alerts for Xid 79 on eu nodes and creating a follow-up ticket: SRE-2026-1245.

noah-eng-runtime: ETA for patching eu fleet: within 48 hours, will target a low-traffic window and coordinate maintenance. I'll post a maintenance notice to customers and link it here.

lisa-support: Closing interim loop — dbg-987654 bundle and pod/node logs attached. If you see any new failures, pls paste request id + Rw-Trace header and we'll reopen immediately. Thanks all. :rocket:
